ex.en: Drivers who ignore traffic regulations may lose their licence for several months.
ex.zh: 无视交通法规的司机可能会被吊销驾照数月。

words.note: regulation 表「规章」时多用复数；regulate 是动词「管理、调节」。

ex.en: All new products must conform to strict safety standards before they go on sale.
ex.zh: 所有新产品上市前都必须符合严格的安全标准。

words.note: conform 常接 to：conform to rules/standards。

ex.en: Regular exercise helps improve blood circulation and keeps the heart healthy.
ex.zh: 经常锻炼有助于改善血液循环，保持心脏健康。

words.note: in circulation 指货币流通或书刊发行；动词形式是 circulate。

ex.en: The restaurant is famous for serving authentic Sichuan food at reasonable prices.
ex.zh: 这家餐厅以价格合理、口味正宗的川菜闻名。

words.note: authentic 强调「真品、正宗」，与 genuine 近义，常形容食物与文物。

ex.en: The mere thought of speaking in public makes her hands shake.
ex.zh: 一想到当众讲话，她的手就发抖。

words.note: mere 置于名词前加强语气，相当于 only，常含「不过…而已」。

ex.en: We booked accommodation near the station so we could walk to the train.
ex.zh: 我们在车站附近订了住处，这样就能步行去坐火车。

words.note: 英式不可数、无复数；美式常用 accommodations。

ex.en: It was evident from her face that she had been crying all night.
ex.zh: 从她脸上明显看出她哭了一整夜。

words.note: it is evident that 后接从句；副词 evidently 表「显然」。

ex.en: They moved to a quiet suburb after their second child was born.
ex.zh: 第二个孩子出生后，他们搬到了安静的郊区。

words.note: the suburbs 泛指郊区；sub-（下、次）+ urb（城市）。

ex.en: Children carved a pumpkin into a funny face for the autumn festival.
ex.zh: 孩子们把南瓜刻成一张滑稽的脸，迎接秋季节日。

words.note: pumpkin 作定语常见于 pumpkin pie、pumpkin soup。

ex.en: Loud music late at night really annoys the neighbours in this building.
ex.zh: 深夜大声放音乐确实会打扰这栋楼的邻居。

words.note: annoy 指反复打扰使人恼火；be annoyed with sb。

ex.en: He professed to know nothing about the missing money when the police questioned him.
ex.zh: 警察询问时，他声称对失踪的钱一无所知。

words.note: profess 比 say 正式，含「公开声称」，常暗示未必真实。

ex.en: Students under great psychological pressure often find it hard to sleep well.
ex.zh: 心理压力大的学生常常睡不好觉。

words.note: psycho-（心灵）+ logy（学科）；名词是 psychology。

ex.en: The witness gave a credible account of what happened that night.
ex.zh: 那位目击者对当晚发生的事做了可信的陈述。

words.note: credible 是「可信的」，credulous 是「轻信的」，注意区分。

ex.en: The theory sounds reasonable but lacks empirical evidence from real classrooms.
ex.zh: 这个理论听起来合理，但缺乏真实课堂的实证证据。

words.note: empirical 强调以观察、实验为依据，与 theoretical 相对。

ex.en: The company committed itself to cutting carbon emissions by thirty percent.
ex.zh: 该公司承诺将碳排放量削减百分之三十。

words.note: commit a crime 是固定搭配；be committed to 后接名词。

ex.en: The government raised interest rates to curb rising inflation.
ex.zh: 政府提高利率以抑制不断上升的通货膨胀。

words.note: curb 作动词表「抑制」，多接 inflation、crime、emissions 等。

ex.en: The truck crashed into a tree and blocked the road for hours.
ex.zh: 卡车撞到树上，把路堵了好几个小时。

words.note: crash into 后接撞上的物体；作名词常指车祸或市场崩溃。

ex.en: The main character in the novel is a young doctor working in a small town.
ex.zh: 这部小说的主人公是在小镇工作的一位年轻医生。

words.note: character 既可指「性格」，也可指书中「人物」，看上下文判断。

ex.en: The report reflects the concerns of teachers across the country.
ex.zh: 这份报告反映了全国各地教师的关切。

words.note: reflect on 表「认真思考」；表「反映」时主语多为数据、报告。

ex.en: She bought a new outfit for the job interview on Monday.
ex.zh: 她为周一的求职面试买了一套新衣服。

words.note: outfit 指搭配好的一整套服装，比 clothes 更强调成套。

ex.en: She made a major contribution to the success of the project.
ex.zh: 她为项目的成功作出了重大贡献。

words.note: make a contribution to 中 to 是介词，后接名词或动名词。

ex.en: The repair work is ongoing and the road will stay closed until Friday.
ex.zh: 维修工作仍在进行，这条路将封闭到周五。

words.note: ongoing 多作定语，表「仍在进行的」，一般不用 very 修饰。

ex.en: The museum records the massacre of civilians during the war.
ex.zh: 这座博物馆记载了战争期间对平民的屠杀。

words.note: massacre 指大规模屠杀（尤指平民），语气强烈，多见于新闻。

ex.en: The doctor reassured her that the test results were completely normal.
ex.zh: 医生让她放心，检查结果完全正常。

words.note: reassure 强调消除疑虑；re-（再）+ assure（保证）。

ex.en: Someone was banging on the door and shouting my name.
ex.zh: 有人在砰砰敲门，还喊着我的名字。

words.note: bang on 指连续猛敲；bang 也可直接作拟声名词「砰的一声」。

ex.en: A compass needle points north because it follows the earth's magnetic field.
ex.zh: 指南针指向北方，因为它顺着地球磁场。

words.note: 除「磁的」，magnetic 还引申为「有吸引力的」，如 magnetic smile。

ex.en: Eating too much fried food can raise your cholesterol level.
ex.zh: 吃太多油炸食品会升高胆固醇水平。

words.note: cholesterol 不可数，常与 high/low、level 搭配。

ex.en: The satellite has been in orbit around the earth for ten years.
ex.zh: 这颗卫星已在地球轨道上运行十年。

words.note: in orbit 前不加冠词；orbit 作动词可直接接天体名称。

ex.en: The band played for two hours and the crowd loved every song.
ex.zh: 乐队演奏了两个小时，观众喜欢每一首歌。

words.note: band 指乐队时视为整体，谓语可用单数；也可指带子、波段。

ex.en: The difference between the two methods is negligible in practice.
ex.zh: 两种方法在实际应用中的差别微不足道。

words.note: negligible 源于 neglect（忽略），指小到可以忽略不计。
